value.body: An environmental planner works on how land and projects can be developed without harming natural resources or exposing people to hazards. Planning and environmental consultancies, infrastructure firms and development organisations hire them. Day-to-day work includes collecting baseline data, mapping sensitive areas, and drafting sections of impact assessment or master-plan reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Plan, or a degree in environmental science or engineering

items.label: Common tools
items.value: GIS software, Excel, EIA notification and guidelines

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a planning or environmental consultancy as a junior planner or EIA associate, working on project reports under a senior expert. Many continue to an M.Plan in environmental planning for more specialised roles.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: GIS mapping of hazards and sensitive zones
Reading environmental regulations and clearance processes

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: environmental planning lead, EIA coordinator, climate or resilience planner.
Work is project-based and tied to infrastructure and urban development cycles.
Leading EIA studies typically needs accredited experts, which takes years of experience.
